summary: Full end-to-end test (backend pytest + frontend Playwright) of the 3 new MVP screens: Documents & Photo Backup (regression), Social Stats, and Settings/More rewrite (privacy, notifications, backup, automations, integrations). All new frontend screens correctly wire to pre-existing backend routes. Found and fixed 2 real backend bugs (1 security-relevant, pre-existing, unrelated to this session's frontend work). All requested flows tested live via Playwright on the mobile viewport and pass.

critical.issue: FIXED: Refresh token rotation issued a brand-new random 'family' on every rotation instead of preserving the original family, so the reuse-detection cascade (revoke whole family on replay) only revoked the token being replayed, not any tokens rotated afterward — an attacker who stole an old refresh token and got detected could still use the latest rotated token. Root cause: routes/auth.py `refresh()` called `security.issue_pair(user_id)` without passing the family. Fixed by having `consume_refresh()` return `(user_id, family)` and passing `family` through to `issue_pair()`. Verified via test_refresh_rotates_and_old_token_reuse_is_detected which now passes (was failing before the fix, confirmed by isolated -n 0 run).

minor.issue: FIXED: disconnect set status to 'disconnected' while the catalog default (never-connected) is 'not_connected' — two different string values for the same 'off' state. Frontend happens to only check `status === 'connected'` so no user-facing bug, but it's an inconsistent contract. Normalized disconnect to also set 'not_connected'.

TestAIMemory tests intermittently fail (403) ONLY when run with the configured `-n 2 --dist loadscope` xdist workers, because the file's fresh_user fixture is session-scoped but xdist gives each worker its own process/session — TestMe (which PATCHes ai_enabled=True) and TestAIMemory can land on different workers with different user instances, so AIMemory's create call 403s (ai_enabled defaults false for a user that never got patched). Confirmed by running the same file with `-n 0`: all 20 tests pass. This is a pre-existing test-file design issue (not a backend bug) — flagging since pytest.ini explicitly pins -n 2/loadscope and says not to change it; the test file itself should give TestAIMemory its own fixture or not rely on cross-class ordering.

issues: No `testID` attributes anywhere in the codebase (0 matches for `testID` in /app/frontend/app and /app/frontend/src) — all interactive elements use `accessibilityLabel`/`accessibilityRole` instead, which happened to work fine for Playwright web selectors in this session but doesn't follow the project's stated testID convention. Pre-existing, not introduced this session.

Console warning on every load: 'In HTML, <button> cannot be a descendant of <button>' / hydration warning — TouchableOpacity-wrapped interactive elements nested inside another Card's TouchableOpacity render as nested <button> on web. Pre-existing pattern, cosmetic console noise only, no functional breakage observed.

action_items: Consider giving TestAIMemory (and any class relying on a profile patched by an earlier class) its own fresh_user fixture, or scope fresh_user at class-level, so the pre-existing test file is robust to the pinned -n 2 --dist loadscope xdist config.
No action required on the 2 backend bugs fixed this session (refresh-token family propagation, integration disconnect status naming) — both fixed, tested and passing.
No action required on the 3 new screens / Social Stats / Documents regression — all flows tested live and pass.

Social Stats mock data (src/features/social/mockSocialData.ts) is honestly labeled in the screen footer and on the Today SocialCard ('Sample' chip) — good transparency practice, no action needed.

rca_of_issue: Refresh token reuse-detection bug: routes/auth.py's /auth/refresh endpoint called security.issue_pair(user_id) on every rotation without passing forward the original token 'family' UUID, so each rotation started a brand-new family. The reuse-detection logic (revoke all sessions matching a family when a revoked/already-used token is replayed) therefore only ever covered the single family a stolen token belonged to at the moment of replay, not any tokens issued in later rotations. Reproduced with: register -> capture refresh_token_1 -> rotate to refresh_token_2 -> replay refresh_token_1 (correctly detected as reuse, 401) -> then use refresh_token_2 (incorrectly succeeded with 200 instead of the expected 401, since refresh_token_2's family was never revoked). Fixed by threading the family through consume_refresh() -> issue_pair(family=...) so all tokens in a rotation chain share one family and are revoked together on any detected replay.
